Add us on Google Add us on Google It’s easy to have a love-hate relationship with zinc oxide, one of the most common active ingredients in mineral-based sunscreens. On the one hand, zinc oxide offers excellent protection from the sun, but on the other, it can leave a white cast on the face or look heavy or greasy—not ideal if you’re heading into the office or need to hop on a Zoom call. 
 But there’s good news: While researching and testing mineral-based sunscreens, which differ from chemical sunscreens in that they sit on top of the skin and serve as a physical barrier against harmful ultraviolet light, we managed to find multiple options that look natural while still offering much-needed sun protection. Here are our favorites and the reasons we liked them.
 Our Top Pick
 After testing a variety of products, our team agreed that the best mineral sunscreen overall is EltaMD UV Skin Recovery Broad Spectrum SPF 50 Face Sunscreen . They love how easily the sunscreen blends into the skin and protects it from the sun.

 Our Thoughts on EltaMD UV Skin Recovery Broad Spectrum SPF 50 Face Sunscreen
 EltaMD UV Skin Recovery SPF 50 is a mineral-based sunscreen “designed to protect, recover and strengthen even the most sensitive skin—like skin prone to rosacea,” according to the company’s website. Besides the active ingredient, zinc oxide, the formula also contains a ceramide blend that “nourishes and reinforces the skin barrier to minimize future damage, redness, and sensitivity.” This sunscreen is also formulated to have a lightweight texture and help reduce redness.
 Katie, a member of our testing team, tried this sunscreen. She said she has combination skin that can be dry during certain times of the year, and she used this sunscreen prior to spending a lot of time outdoors. “I was incredibly impressed by this sunscreen,” she said, citing the easy-to-use pump bottle, easy blending, and excellent sun protection.
 “It blended incredibly well,” said Katie, adding that it “felt very smooth upon application” and didn’t leave a white cast. She also said her makeup was easy to apply on top of the sunscreen, and “It dried quickly and did not feel greasy or chalky.” Katie rated the application a 5 out of 5, and another 5 out of 5 for the product’s texture and feel. 
 Katie said her skin is generally susceptible to burning when out in the sun, but that EltaMD UV Skin Recovery SPF 50 kept her protected whenever she was outside—though she noted she did reapply every two hours. She rated the protection and practical performance a 5 out of 5.
 “This product did not irritate my skin at all,” said Katie, adding that the product would be well-suited for busy professionals who want something quick and easy to apply and that layers well with makeup without leaving a white cast.

 Our Thoughts on La Roche-Posay Anthelios Mineral SPF 50 Gentle Lotion
 This mineral sunscreen is formulated for use on both face and body, and its active ingredients include both zinc oxide and titanium dioxide. It’s designed to blend easily, and the oil-free formula is meant to leave a soft, non-greasy finish. It’s deemed suitable for all skin types, even sensitive skin.
 A member of our testing team, Reese, who has combination skin and is generally sensitive to sunscreen, tried The La Roche-Posay Anthelios Mineral Sunscreen was fairly time-consuming to apply given the thickness of the product and the initial white cast it leaves behind. It took a good few minutes to rub in the sunscreen so it didn’t appear to have a white residue.” He rated the ease of application a 3 out of 5.
 Despite the initial challenges with application, Reese said, “Once the product was fully absorbed, it did feel smooth on my skin. There was no sticky or greasy residue, and no overbearing smell, which I appreciated.” Reese said he was pleasantly surprised that after the sunscreen absorbed into his skin, “There was no greasy or sticky residue, and the white cast eventually faded over a period of time. I was also planning to be in an area that is buggy, so having a sunscreen that wasn’t dewy or wet after application was a plus for me.” He rated it a 4 out of 5 for its texture and feel.
 When it came to actual sun protection, Reese said, “The wear and durability of this product is where I felt it really shone. It was effective in preventing sunburn, and it did not break down with sweat. I used the product on my arms, neck, and chest and saw a noticeable difference in protection vs. my legs where I used a spray-on sunscreen. After extended use, I did not experience any burning or irritation and felt that the sunscreen held up well.” He rated this sunscreen a 5 out of 5 for its protection and practical performance. 
 Who Should Avoid La Roche-Posay Anthelios Mineral SPF 50 Gentle Lotion
 Overall, Reese said he recommends this sunscreen primarily for the body because “it was a bit too heavy” for his face, required some time to fully rub it in, and left a white cast. For that reason, it’s best suited for professionals who put in as much outdoor time as they do office time and are looking for a full-body sunscreen that offers reliable protection. Anyone looking for a face-specific sunscreen might be better off elsewhere.

We love the ingredients in this mineral sunscreen: non-nano zinc oxide is used to protect the skin from sun damage, while hyaluronic acid hydrates and undaria seaweed delivers antioxidants and amino acids to the skin. 
 Our tester Paige tried the Marine Screen SPF 50 Mineral Sunscreen from OSEA, and gave it a perfect score in most categories. It earned 5 out of 5 in the category of application. “This sunscreen spreads really well and with ease,” she said. “A little goes a long way and it is very light weight.” Paige also noted that this sunscreen layers well under makeup.
 “This sunscreen has a nice natural finish,” Paige continued. Because this mineral sunscreen left her skin looking hydrated but not greasy, she gave it a rating of 5 out of 5 in the category of finish.
 In the category of wear, OSEA’s mineral sunscreen also earned a 5 out of 5. Paige specifically noted the sunscreen stayed comfortable all day, even when her face was sweaty. “It did not change textures or become heavier throughout the day,” she said. “It also didn’t affect the wear time of my makeup.”
 When it came to the protection provided by this mineral sunscreen, Paige had a lot of positive things to report after testing. This is an SPF 50 sunscreen, which is adequate protection for many skin types in direct sunlight. “It held up really well,” Paige said. “I could go a long time without having to reapply. I did not experience any redness, burning or issues from the sun or reacting with sweat, which was a plus.”

 Why the Right Sunscreen Matters to Professionals 
 Dermatologists commonly recommend wearing sunscreen every day, but because some formulations leave a greasy residue or white cast, it can be challenging to find a product that offers the necessary coverage and is suitable for work. 
 Mineral sunscreens can be especially challenging from an aesthetic standpoint, as zinc oxide—a common active ingredient in mineral-based products—is known for leaving a white cast. However, today’s marketplace offers plenty of sunscreen options, and our testing showed that even mineral-based sunscreens can offer more natural-looking coverage and layer well with makeup and moisturizer. 
 The sunscreens in our lineup can be seamlessly added to a morning routine and worn all day at work without seeming to scream “I’m wearing sunscreen.”
 How We Tested and Selected the Best Mineral Sunscreen
 Here’s what we took into account when choosing and testing products. 
 Texture and Feel
 Some sunscreens are thicker, others feel silky, and some might even feel liquidy. We noted each product’s texture and how it felt during and after application.
 Formula
 We focused on mineral sunscreens for this testing, and we also looked at the so-called “inactive ingredients,” which sometimes include ingredients that the company says confer certain benefits.
 Application and Coverage
 Sunscreens don’t always spread smoothly when applied, so we asked our testers to note how easy the application process was and whether they felt the sunscreen provided good coverage without requiring a lot of additional product.
 Skin Compatibility 
 Our testers, who have a range of skin types, reported on how well a product worked on their particular skin type.
 Value
 Price isn’t always the most important criterion when choosing a face sunscreen, but we know it matters to many people.  How to Find the Best Mineral Sunscreen for You
 Here’s what to consider when searching for the best mineral sunscreen to fit into your daily routine.
 Your Skin Type
 Everyone’s skin type is unique, so make sure to consider your skin’s needs. For example, those with acne or rosacea might prefer a product formulated to be suitable for those skin conditions, while those with oily skin might prefer an oil-free formula. 
 SPF Level
 Every product we tested had an SPF of 50, but there’s a wide range of options available—so consider what SPF you’re targeting, and keep in mind that many people don’t apply as much sunscreen as recommended by experts, so the actual amount of protection can be lower than the stated SPF.
 Finish
 Some sunscreens have a matte finish, while others leave a dewier look. Think about whether you have a preference, and if so, shop accordingly.
 What to Avoid in Mineral Sunscreen 
 Dr. Sumeet Thareja , a board-certified dermatologist, Mohs surgeon, and founder at Indigo Dermatology, said mineral sunscreen works right away, is ideal for sensitive skin, and provides broad-spectrum UVA and UVB protection. But there are downsides as well, according to Thareja, who explained, “Mineral sunscreens leave a noticeable white film on your skin and tend to feel heavy or thicker. It can also rub off quicker.”
 Here’s what he said to look for and avoid in a mineral sunscreen.
 Look for certain active ingredients: ”You should look for the active ingredients of zinc oxide and titanium dioxide,” said Thareja, adding, “Tinted formulas can help cut down on the white cast.”
 Look for protection from both UVA and UVB rays: You should also look for “broad spectrum” on the label, said Thareja, meaning that sunscreen is designed to protect your skin from both ultraviolet A (UVA) and ultraviolet B (UVB) rays.
 Avoid spray sunscreens: “Avoid aerosol sprays which can cause breathing issues for sensitive groups,” said Thareja. Plus, spray sunscreen may cause inadequate application and uneven coverage.
 Avoid ingredients that can irritate sensitive skin: Thareja also recommended avoiding synthetic fragrances and dyes if you have sensitive skin.
 Fortune’s Final Thoughts
 EltaMD UV Skin Recovery Broad Spectrum SPF 50 Face Sunscreen was our choice for best overall mineral sunscreen, and we think it’s ideal for career-focused individuals because it’s easy to apply and feels nice on the skin, offers excellent sun protection, and doesn’t leave a white cast—so you won’t get any funny looks in your meetings. It also layers well with makeup and works well on sensitive skin. This sunscreen requires minimal effort to apply and gives excellent skin protection, which is a great ROI if you ask us. 
 Frequently asked questions
 What is a good lightweight mineral sunscreen? 
 After testing, we named EltaMD UV Skin Recovery Broad Spectrum SPF 50 Face Sunscreen the best overall mineral sunscreen, but we had a lot of strong contenders in the lineup—so there are many great options to choose from depending on your personal preferences.
 Do dermatologists prefer chemical or mineral sunscreen? 
 According to Thareja, “The ideal choice depends on your personal skin type, daily activities, and cosmetic preferences. Mineral is best if you have sensitive, reactive, or acne-prone skin. Chemical is better if you prefer a transparent finish, lightweight feel, or heavy-duty water resistance for sports. Both protect your skin effectively when applied correctly.” Thareja advised, “Find whatever works for you to make sunscreen part of your daily routine.”
 What are the disadvantages of mineral sunscreen? 
 Thareja said mineral sunscreens often leave a white film on your skin and can feel thicker than chemical sunscreens, plus product transfer may be more visible with mineral sunscreens.
 Is it safe to wear mineral sunscreen every day? 
 “Yes, mineral sunscreens are safe to use every day,” said Thareja, noting, “I encourage everyone to use sunscreen daily and reapply to prevent sunburns, aging, and skin cancer.”
